---
title: Write edges in a working copy
description: Link items, move an edge's end and check a write first with marfa device, and learn of a refusal offline, before anything is queued.
---

An [edge](/build/edges) points from one item to another. In a working copy, an edge write is judged against what the copy holds before it's queued, so a script offline learns of a refusal when it writes, not at the next drain. The commands here assume a copy that [Write in a working copy](/build/write-in-a-working-copy) has filled, named by `--db` or `MARFA_DB`.

**An edge write needs a copy that is whole and current.** While the copy fills, or once it's `stale`, every edge write is refused `hydration_incomplete` and nothing is queued: write it again once the copy is current.

## Link two items

`marfa device edges create` queues an edge. This one puts a novel in its series, with the series as the from item:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device edges create --from-id <series-id> --to-id <book-id> --type parent-of
```

```text
queued create_edge 01a1f122-b1bb-7262-810d-4f526ace3cb7 as 01a1f122-c3f4-7487-9dc5-215a47a5c540
```

</Terminal>

The first ID is the from item's and the second the queued write's. `marfa device edges list <id>` reads the edges from an item and `edges to <id>` the edges to it, each with the edge's own ID and its version, which is `0` until the server answers the create.

## Move an edge

`marfa device edges update` changes an edge's properties or moves one of its ends, and names the version it was based on, as an item update does. This moves the book to another series:

```bash
marfa device edges update <edge-id> --version 1 --from-id <other-series-id>
```

**A move changes one end, and only while the end that stays holds one edge of the type.** A `parent-of` edge is one-to-many: a series has many books, and a book has one series. Moving the from end keeps the book, which holds one `parent-of` edge, so a book moves to another series that way. Moving the to end keeps the series, which holds many, so it's refused `validation_error` ([`edges/move-many`](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/edges.md#edgesmove-many)). Create the edge you want and delete the old one instead. A move of both ends is always refused.

**After a drain sends a move of an edge's from item, the copy expires.** The move can change what the key reaches, so the drain sends every write queued behind it and then ends `copy_expired` once. Run `marfa device hydrate` again to rebuild the copy ([`queue-and-verdicts/edge-from-move-one-expiry`](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/queue-and-verdicts.md#queue-and-verdictsedge-from-move-one-expiry)).

## What the copy refuses

**The copy refuses an edge write the instance would refuse, before it queues anything.** An edge from an item to itself is refused `edge_cycle` first, whatever the copy holds. Then it judges an edge create, a move and the edges of an item create in the order the instance does, and gives the first refusal it finds:

| Order | Refusal | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | An end is in the bin | `item_not_found` |
| 2 | An end's type isn't one the edge type admits, or the edge would nest under a flat edge type | `edge_constraint_violation` |
| 3 | A second edge of the type between the same two items | `edge_constraint_violation`, with `details.constraint` `duplicate` |
| 4 | A second edge at an end that holds one edge of the type: either end of a one-to-one type, the to end of a one-to-many type, the from end of a many-to-one type | `edge_constraint_violation`, with `details.constraint` `cardinality` |
| 5 | A cycle through other items | `edge_cycle` |

The [Edges catalog](/catalog/edges) lists each edge type's cardinality. The refusal carries the instance's code and `details`, such as `edge_type`, `from_id`, `to_id` and `constraint`, so a script handles it as it would the instance's answer. Under `--json`, the error on standard error holds them under `local`, and the command exits `1`:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device edges create --from-id <other-series-id> --to-id <book-id> --type parent-of --json
```

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation","message":"validation (edge_constraint_violation): Edge \"parent-of\" is one-to-many on the to side; the to item already has an inbound edge of this type","server":null,"local":{"code":"edge_constraint_violation","details":{"edge_type":"parent-of","to_id":"01a1f122-b1e6-74e9-b95c-346ac2b271ec","constraint":"cardinality"}},"retry_after_seconds":null},"exit":1}
```

</Terminal>

A script that writes an edge again after an uncertain answer can treat `duplicate` as success.

**The copy counts edges as the instance will hold them once the queue is sent**: the edges it holds, plus each waiting create or move where it will stand, minus each edge a waiting delete removes. A write the instance refused counts for nothing, and a move onto the end the edge already holds changes nothing.

**What the copy doesn't hold, the instance judges.** An edge type, an end or an edge outside the copy's slice can't be judged, so the write is queued and the instance gives its verdict when it's sent. A write it refuses then stays in the queue as `refused`, with its body.

## Check before you write

`marfa device edges check` answers what the matching create would, and `edges check-move` what the matching move would. Neither queues anything. Ask before a person confirms a choice, such as dropping a book onto another series:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa device edges check-move <edge-id> --from-id <other-series-id> --json
```

```json
{
  "refused": false
}
```

</Terminal>

A check that finds a refusal exits as the write would, with the same code and details. **Finding nothing isn't the instance's verdict**: it judges the write once it's sent. An app on the [Swift SDK](/swift-sdk/items#edges) checks an edge with `edges.check(from:to:type:)` and a move with `edges.check(_:moving:)`, and reads the same `details`.

The rules behind this guide are in the section on [an edge the server would refuse](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/queue-and-verdicts.md#an-edge-the-server-would-refuse) in the queue and verdicts chapter of the contract, and the order is [`queue-and-verdicts/edge-self-loop`](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/queue-and-verdicts.md#queue-and-verdictsedge-self-loop) and [`queue-and-verdicts/edge-refusal-order`](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/queue-and-verdicts.md#queue-and-verdictsedge-refusal-order).
